questions.q: Which column in sys.dm_exec_query_stats represents cumulative CPU time across all executions of a cached plan?
options: avg_duration
execution_count
total_worker_time
total_logical_reads
questions.explain: total_worker_time is CPU time in microseconds, summed across every execution the plan has seen since being cached.

questions.q: Why might a query that runs in 5 milliseconds be a bigger overall problem than a report that takes 30 seconds?
options: SQL Server always prioritizes long-running queries for eviction
Fast queries always use more memory than slow ones
If it runs 100,000 times a day, its total aggregate cost can far exceed the report's one-time cost
Short queries can never appear in the plan cache
questions.explain: Total resource consumption multiplies per-execution cost by execution count, so high-frequency cheap queries can dominate aggregate cost.

questions.q: When should a DBA sort by average rather than total resource consumption?
options: Only when Query Store is disabled
Never — average is meaningless in SQL Server
When investigating one specific complaint about one specific report's worst execution
Always — average is the correct first-pass triage metric
questions.explain: Average finds the single worst individual execution, which is useful for a targeted complaint but misleading for first-pass, server-wide triage.

questions.q: Which column would you sort by to find the queries doing the most I/O in aggregate?
options: total_worker_time
total_logical_reads
is_percent_growth
plan_generation_num
questions.explain: total_logical_reads is the cumulative pages read from buffer cache across all executions — the I/O-bound counterpart to total_worker_time's CPU focus.

questions.q: What is standard practice when triaging 'the server is slow' using sys.dm_exec_query_stats?
options: Run the query sorted by total CPU and separately by total logical reads, and compare the two lists
Restart the SQL Server service before running any DMV query
Only ever check total_worker_time and ignore I/O entirely
Immediately run DBCC CHECKDB before checking resource consumption
questions.explain: Comparing the CPU-sorted and I/O-sorted lists highlights queries that are expensive on both axes — the ones worth tuning first.
